principle: Normalise only values that are provably environment-dependent and carry no behavioural information. Field presence, JSON types, enum strings and model numbers are never normalised.

rules.target: fields hmiTime, t, lastUpdate, timestamp; patterns dd.mm.yyyy HH:MM:SS and ISO-8601
rules.rationale: Wall-clock time is set by the environment, not by the HMI logic. The HMI's *format* is still compared because the surrounding string shape is preserved.

Per-database session identity; regenerated when /db is recreated. Within-run stability is asserted separately (scenario 02, capture + equals_ref), so normalisation does not hide a per-request random id.
Bearer token minted per request by the harness (bin2hex(random_bytes(32))).
Exact latency is CPU/scheduler dependent. Order-of-magnitude is kept so a gross regression (e.g. 30 s timeout) still shows up.

Append-only rows: the config table gets a new row (id+1) on every HMI start and machineCounters.powerOnCycles increments per boot. The delta is recorded separately (reboot.pre_state/post_state, config hash excluding the id line), so monotonicity is still observable.
rules.evidence: observed: configId 1->2 after one restart; HsgConfig.json carries the same id

rules.rationale: Interface MACs are assigned by the virtual NIC / DTB and are not HMI behaviour.
The harness uses a dedicated port block; a reconstruction may listen elsewhere.
Addresses come from the QEMU user-network (10.0.2.x) or the virtual AP (192.168.4.1).
Log timestamps are monotonic since process start.
Absolute epoch values depend on when the run happened.

The ring buffer is drained by concurrent writers; entry order within a drain is not stable. Content is additionally reduced to a structural digest (count/levels/categories) because the buffer is a history of ambient boot events, not a function of the scripted inputs.
rules.evidence: observed: two consecutive runs differed in ring content

explicitly_not_normalised: reply type strings, refId echo, data.success, enum values (grindState, grindFailure, setupWizardState, language)
the 59 driver-config and 48 driver-state keys, including numeric calibration constants
HTTP status codes, error bodies, and side-effect file names (after removing embedded timestamps)
sysfs values (LEDs, backlight, gpio), because those are the actuator contract
database row counts and settings keys/values
the *presence* of an esp.json heartbeat and its order-of-magnitude rate (only the exact frame count is dropped)
